title: 2023 HMMT February Geometry Problem 2
statement: Points \(X, Y\), and \(Z\) lie on a circle with center \(O\) such that \(X Y=12\). Points \(A\) and \(B\) lie on segment \(X Y\) such that \(O A=A Z=Z B=B O=5\). Compute \(A B\).

solutions.text: Let the midpoint of \(X Y\) be \(M\). Because \(O A Z B\) is a rhombus, \(O Z \perp A B\), so \(M\) is the midpoint of \(A B\) as well. Since \(O M=\frac{1}{2} O X, \triangle O M X\) is a \(30-60-90\) triangle, and since \(X M=6\), \(O M=2 \sqrt{3}\). Since \(O A=5\), the Pythagorean theorem gives \(A M=\sqrt{13}\), so \(A B=2 \sqrt{13}\).
